summary: Custom types like AnsibleUnicode, AnsibleSequence and AnsibleMapping now have new subclasses of native Python types; they mostly behave the same, but libraries that mishandle builtin subclasses may need native conversion.
questions: What happened to AnsibleUnicode in ansible-core 2.19?
Why does a Python library choke on Ansible variables in my plugin?
Do I need to convert Ansible variables to native types in plugins?

answer_card.title: Ansible custom data types changed
answer_card.answer_md:
Variables used to appear as types such as `AnsibleUnicode` (str), `AnsibleSequence` (list) and `AnsibleMapping` (dict). These and others now have new subclasses of native Python types. They mostly behave the same, but some Python libraries don't handle builtin subclasses properly, so custom plugins using those libraries may need to convert to native types first.
